item.title: Reinstalling WSL2: Migrating a Research and Development Environment from Ubuntu 22.04 to Ubuntu 26.04
item.description:
Recently, I reinstalled the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2), migrated my existing Ubuntu 22.04 development environment to Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and reconfigured my research and development tools, including C++, CUDA, Python, and GitHub.

The immediate reason for this reinstallation was disk space. My computer has only one 1 TB SSD, and the old WSL installation was taking up nearly 500 GB. Upon investigation, I found that the problem wasn’t entirely due to the WSL virtual disk itself, but rather to the long-term accumulation of research code, compilation outputs, and numerical experiment results.

I’ve decided to take this opportunity to reorganize my entire development environment and document any noteworthy configuration details.

item.title: Poisson Manifolds
item.description: Abstract. A smooth manifold tells us what it means to move and differentiate, but it does not determine a dynamics. A Poisson structure adds an antisymmetric bracket on smooth functions that turns each function into a vector field and each Hamiltonian into an evolution law. This post introduces that idea from canonical Hamiltonian mechanics, passes from the algebraic bracket to the intrinsic Poisson bivector, explains the Jacobi identity and its coordinate form, and shows how a possibly degenerate Poisson manifold decomposes into symplectic leaves. The main examples are canonical phase space, two-dimensional Poisson structures, and the Lie–Poisson structure on \(\mathbb{R}^3\).

item.title: Smooth Manifolds
item.description: Abstract. A smooth manifold is a space that may be globally curved or topologically complicated while remaining locally indistinguishable from Euclidean space. This post introduces the subject from scratch, with a notation guide and a sequence of geometric illustrations. We begin with topology, charts, transition maps, and atlases; then define smooth functions and smooth maps without assuming that the manifold sits inside a larger Euclidean space. From there, we construct tangent and cotangent spaces, differentials, vector fields, integral curves, flows, and Lie brackets. The sphere serves as a recurring example, allowing each abstract definition to be compared with familiar geometry. The central theme is that coordinates make calculations possible, while compatibility under coordinate changes makes the resulting mathematics intrinsic.

item.title: Korn's Inequality
item.description: Abstract. In elasticity and viscous-fluid mechanics, energy controls the symmetric part of a vector-field gradient, whereas compactness and well-posedness usually require control of the full gradient. Korn’s inequality bridges this gap after the invisible rigid motions have been removed. This post explains the geometric obstruction, states the principal bounded-domain estimates, and gives a detailed proof of the quotient form using the Poincaré–Lions inequality in \(H^{-1}\).

item.title: The Gelfand Triple and Weak Laplacian
item.description: Abstract. The classical Laplacian asks for two derivatives, but weak solutions of elliptic and parabolic equations often possess only one square-integrable derivative. This post introduces the canonical Gelfand triple \(H_0^1(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^2(\Omega) \hookrightarrow H^{-1}(\Omega)\) from scratch. We explain what each embedding means, construct the weak Dirichlet Laplacian as a bounded map from \(H_0^1(\Omega)\) to \(H^{-1}(\Omega)\), distinguish it from the unbounded Laplacian on \(L^2(\Omega)\), and show why this framework is natural for the Poisson and heat equations.

item.title: Radiation Transport Equation
item.description: Radiation transport problems involve the study of how radiant energy propagates through a background medium and the processes by which it interacts with matter.

item.title: Landau equation
item.description: The Landau equation models the evolution of the distribution of charged particles in a collisional plasma, particularly in regimes where grazing collisions dominate. Alongside the Boltzmann equation, it is considered one of the most important equations in kinetic theory. Recently, it has garned renewed interest in computational plasma physics due to its significant applications in fusion reactors.
